name: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision

entry.name: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
entry.note: The vision course that trained a generation; lectures, notes, and assignments public

covers: practical engineering tricks for deep neural networks
reading.format: The course is delivered through in-person lectures with recorded videos, office hours, and assessed via Python assignments, a midterm, and a final course project.
reading.summary: This is a 10-week Stanford course on deep learning for computer vision. It focuses on end-to-end models for visual recognition tasks such as image classification. Students implement and train neural networks and complete a final project applying large networks to real-world vision problems. Finishing the course provides practical skills for setting up deep learning tasks and training deep neural networks.
reading.audience: The course is intended for students who have programming experience, are comfortable with derivatives and matrix-vector operations, and have an intuitive understanding of basic probability and Gaussian distributions.
reading.prerequisites: Familiarity with Python and numpy, programming experience, comfort with derivatives and matrix-vector operations, and an intuitive understanding of basic probability, Gaussian distributions, mean, and standard deviation.
